Model evaluation¶

The first notebook checked that the data and model files are what we say they are. This one asks how good the detector really is, and how far the numbers can be trusted. Everything is computed from files committed in this repository, so it reruns offline in a few seconds. The figures are also saved as PNG, SVG and PDF in figures/, each with the CSV table behind it.

How a photo is scored. The detector runs on the whole photo, and each class keeps its best box confidence. The photo's call is the class with the highest score, or no detection when no box reaches 0.25, the same cut the live feed uses. Every proportion carries a 95% Wilson interval, which stays sensible near 0% and 100%.

Two photo sets.

Set Photos Where from Seen in training?
Farm test 679 Zenodo 4628934, the held-out 10% of the training collection No, but same farms and visits
Lab-confirmed (PCR) 1,255 Zenodo 5801834, a separate collection whose labels were confirmed by PCR No

The detector is the default close-up model, models/dropping4-laptop, at 640 pixels.

In [1]:
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, display
import hc_viz as hv

hv.style()
pd.set_option("display.precision", 3)
farm, pcr = ev.scored("farm_test_predictions"), ev.scored("pcr_predictions")
show = lambda name: display(Image(filename=str(ev.FIGURES / f"{name}.png"), width=900))
print(f"farm test {len(farm)} photos, lab-confirmed {len(pcr)} photos")

farm test 679 photos, lab-confirmed 1255 photos

1. Training: measured, not read by eye¶

The first notebook could only read the training curves from images. The per-epoch logs are now committed, so the curves below are drawn from results.csv.

In [2]:
t = ev.fig_training(); show("05_training_curves"); t
Out[2]:
epochs best epoch (val mAP50-95) best val mAP50-95 lowest val loss epoch val loss at end vs lowest train loss at end vs lowest
run
Close-up model (dropping4-laptop) 69 49 0.602 60 0.032 0.0
Pen-scale model (dropping4-pen) 38 28 0.462 27 0.000 0.0

Reading. In both runs validation loss stops improving while training loss keeps falling, which is the usual start of overfitting. Early stopping keeps the best validation epoch (49 for the close-up model, 28 by mAP50-95 for the pen model), so the shipped weights come from before the gap opens. The pen run's sharp drop in training loss at epoch 31 happens when mosaic augmentation switches off for the last 10 planned epochs (close_mosaic: 10 of 40 in its args.yaml). Validation does not follow, so it is not a real gain.

2. The headline: farm test against new photos¶

In [3]:
t = ev.fig_recall(farm, pcr); show("07_recall_by_class"); t.pivot(index="class", columns="set", values=["recall", "ci_low", "ci_high"]).round(3)
Out[3]:
recall ci_low ci_high
set farm pcr farm pcr farm pcr
class
all 0.979 0.671 0.966 0.644 0.988 0.696
cocci 1.000 0.697 0.982 0.649 1.000 0.741
healthy 0.976 0.634 0.944 0.582 0.990 0.683
ncd 0.946 0.419 0.823 0.351 0.985 0.491
salmo 0.969 0.814 0.938 0.770 0.985 0.851

Reading. On held-out farm photos the model calls 97.9% of photos right (95% CI 96.6 to 98.8%). On the lab-confirmed photos from a separate collection it calls 67.1% right (64.4 to 69.6%). The intervals are far apart, so this is not noise. Newcastle-like drops the most, to 41.9%. It is also the class with by far the fewest photos (376 in the whole collection, against over 2,000 for each of the others). The farm test number describes photos like the training photos, not photos in general. That is the number to quote with care.

In [4]:
t = ev.fig_confusion(farm, pcr); show("06_confusion_matrices")

Reading. On the new photos most errors are not swaps between diseases. They are photos called healthy or salmonella-like by mistake, and photos with no detection at all (20% of healthy, 27% of Newcastle-like). Healthy photos in the training set show the dropping small in the frame (notebook 1, median 2.6% of the photo against 12 to 22% for the others). Different framing in the new collection is one likely reason for the misses, but this notebook does not prove it.

3. Can the model say when it is unsure?¶

In [5]:
t = ev.fig_coverage(farm, pcr); show("08_accuracy_vs_coverage"); t
Out[5]:
set threshold answered accuracy of answers
0 farm 0.25 0.994 0.985
1 farm 0.50 0.946 0.992
2 farm 0.80 0.697 0.994
3 pcr 0.25 0.852 0.788
4 pcr 0.50 0.670 0.826
5 pcr 0.80 0.278 0.874

Reading. If the model only answers when its best box clears a threshold, its answers get more reliable. On new photos, raising the threshold from 0.25 to 0.80 lifts accuracy of the answers from 78.8% to 87.4%, but it then answers only 27.8% of photos. A higher threshold does not close the gap to the farm test. It is a fair way to make the alerts quieter and more trustworthy, at the cost of asking a person to look at more photos.

Note that the right end of each curve (the model always answers, no threshold) is higher than section 2. There a photo under 0.25 counts as wrong, here it keeps its best guess.

Reading. Both curves sit above the diagonal: when the best box says 0.6, the photo is right more than 60% of the time. So the box score is a ranking, not a probability. It must not be shown to a farmer as "60% sure" without calibrating it first, for example by fitting a temperature or isotonic map on the validation split. Bins with under 10 photos are labelled in the chart and should not be read.

4. Are test photos also in training?¶

The split is random by photo, so the same picture saved twice could land on both sides. Every farm photo was reduced to a 256-bit difference hash (audit_images.py farm). For each test photo the chart shows how many bits differ from its closest training photo.

In [7]:
t = ev.fig_duplicates(farm); show("10_duplicates_across_split"); display(t); print("exact copies by class:"); t.attrs["by_class"]
photos correct accuracy ci_low ci_high
test photos
all 679 665 0.979 0.966 0.988
exact copies of a training photo 49 49 1.000 NaN NaN
without the copies 630 616 0.978 0.963 0.987 
exact copies by class:
Out[7]:
cls
healthy     1
cocci      19
salmo      29
ncd         0
Name: count, dtype: int64

Reading. 49 test photos (7.2%) are exact copies of a training photo. The closest pair is saved in figures/pairs/ and is the same image under two file names. The copies are all called right, but removing them barely moves the score (97.9% to 97.8%), so they are not what makes the farm number high. The bigger issue is the one section 2 shows: the farm test shares farms and visits with training, while the new collection does not.

Fix for the next training run: drop exact duplicates before splitting, and split by visit or farm if the publisher can provide it.

5. Pen scale and the live clip¶

The close-up model was built on photos where the dropping fills the frame. In a pen camera a dropping is a few pixels wide. dropping4-pen is a fine-tune on pen-scale views, tested on cameras it never saw in training.

In [8]:
t = ev.fig_pen(); show("11_pen_scale_before_after"); t
Out[8]:
before after
metric
Pen scale: droppings found (recall) 0.289 0.798
Pen scale: flags that are droppings (precision) 0.112 0.927
Pen scale: mAP50, any class 0.067 0.875
Pen scale: mAP50, right class 0.027 0.651
Close-up photos: mAP50 0.873 0.853

Reading. At pen scale the close-up model finds 29% of droppings and only 11% of its flags are droppings. The fine-tune finds 80% with 93% of flags right, and it loses 0.02 mAP50 on close-ups. The pen test droppings are real Machuve droppings pasted onto real pen frames, so this measures finding small droppings on real floors, not on naturally occurring ones.

Out[9]:

Reading. In three held-out minutes of Pen A1 video with 10 droppings placed at known times, the live pipeline (spot finder, then detector) flags 7, five of them within 2 seconds, and raises no false flags. One Newcastle-like, one coccidiosis-like and one healthy dropping are missed. Ten droppings is a small sample, so read it as a working demonstration, not a rate.

What this supports and what it does not¶

Claim Evidence Verdict
The detector separates the four classes on photos like its training photos 97.9% (96.6 to 98.8%) on 679 held-out farm photos Supported
It does the same on new photos 67.1% (64.4 to 69.6%) on 1,255 lab-confirmed photos Not supported
The farm score is inflated by duplicates 49 exact copies, removing them changes 97.9% to 97.8% Not supported, the effect is small
Its confidence is a probability Both sets sit above the diagonal Not supported, it needs calibrating
It finds small droppings in pen video pen fine-tune recall 0.80, precision 0.93, unseen cameras Supported, on pasted droppings
It works live 7 of 10 placed droppings, 0 false flags Demonstrated, small sample
